rationale: This inscription is an inventory of sacred and public property on the island of Delos, dating to the period of the Athenian Amphictyony (342-340 BC). It lists a wide variety of items, including bronze and silver vessels (craters, cauldrons, foot-basins), naval equipment (trireme parts, rudders, ropes), and military gear (breastplates, greaves, swords). The text frequently notes the condition of the items, specifically if they are broken (kateagos), and records their weights, which was a standard practice for administrative accountability in Greek sanctuaries.
